decks.linkedin:
Most enquiries don't die on price. They die in the gap between the message and the first reply.

Across the businesses we work with, every lead makes the same six stops:

1. Arrival: scattered across WhatsApp, DMs, missed calls and forms
2. Acknowledgement: the one gap that costs nothing to close
3. Qualification: three questions (what, when, who)
4. Routing: hot, warm and cold need different speeds
5. Follow-up: most deals are won after attempt four
6. Record: if it isn't logged, it didn't happen

The three leaks show up every time: the night gap, no named owner, no record.

decks.title: How you pay for AI work is changing
decks.instagram:
Per-seat pricing made sense when people did the work. It doesn't when the work runs at 2am.

Three models are replacing it: build fee, usage and outcome. Here's what each one is best for, and the four protections to ask for before you sign anything usage-based.

Save this for your next proposal review.

Comment PRICING and we'll tell you which one fits your volume.

#aiautomation #pricing #smallbusiness #aiagents #yourbrand
decks.linkedin:
Per-seat pricing is losing its logic. When an agent does the work, a seat count stops measuring anything real.

Three models are taking its place:

→ Build fee: pay once, own it. Best for steady, predictable volume.
→ Usage: pay per run. Best for volume that moves month to month.
→ Outcome: pay per result. Best when the result is clear and countable.

If you go usage-based, ask for four things in writing: a monthly cap, an alert at 70%, a kill switch, and a dry-run estimate.

Which model are your vendors pushing you toward?
